issues.claim: The way-and-channel table's row (b), its gates cell (base l. 2914), still moves a hand way's crossing of a trace 'along the deck to the nearest crossing clear of the strip'. The laws admit a gate under an aqueduct's arch in an over crossing whose spans clear it (law 1 (5), l. 2724-2725) and take a stroke's value to the nearest lawful shape (law 2 (a), l. 2810-2811; law 3); §7.1's row (VF7-HND-01's fix) reads 'its crossing of a trace to the nearest at which §2.7's laws admit its gate' (l. 11340), as T110-2 (5) does (l. 19478-19479). Where the nearest admitted crossing lies inside the strip, the example and the laws differ; the outcome table and the bar carry the laws, so nothing built or tested changes.
issues.required_change: §2.7's way-and-channel table, row (b), its gates cell (l. 2914): "such a crossing of the trace is moved along the deck to the nearest crossing clear of the strip (`bend.raised.underSpan`, its wall form)" → "such a crossing of the trace is moved along the deck to the nearest crossing at which these laws admit its gate (law 1 (5), law 2 (a), law 3; `bend.raised.underSpan`, its wall form)".

issues.kind: READERS (law 4's undo refusal has no home in §7.1's outcome table or §7.4)
issues.claim: Law 4 (l. 2864-2867) refuses an undo or redo 'where law 1 would not then hold ... naming each later live event whose structure or lock it would meet'. §7.4 *Independence* (l. 12019-12022, 12030-12040) holds a later event dependent only by touched sets, effective-scope faces and inputs, and calls 'the state after a permitted undo ... the fold of the log without its target' (l. 12041); §7.1's undo row (l. 11306), the one home of every refusal cause (l. 11280), names only 'dependent live events (§7.4 *Independence*)'. Part P's PRB7D-LCK-17 case (adjudication-r7.md l. 3122; probe-r7d-locks.md l. 513-536) passes that check: a declared aqueduct with all spans open deleted, a wall drawn through where its supports stood, the owner's Undo this of the delete (V09 §4.20.3 (4)) - touched sets disjoint, the exact inverse standing supports in the band (law 1 (2)). The dry run validates §5.3's law-1 row on every event (l. 11270-11271; l. 9940), so nothing commits and law 1 holds either way, but no outcome row maps the failure: one build refuses refuse.undo.dependent naming the drawWall with Build it again (V09 l. 3101), another an unmapped invariant failure (at most refuse.bug, l. 11328) naming nothing. No bar runs it: T110-4 (c) undoes each hand op at once (l. 19581, 19590-19592). Every outcome keeps law 1 and passes the check: minor. A lock's part is J150's and is left out.
issues.required_change: 1. §7.4 *Independence* (l. 12020-12022): "disjoint from the target's touched set and from the target's effective-scope faces dilated by one ring of adjacent faces at the coarsest level either touches." → "disjoint from the target's touched set and from the target's effective-scope faces dilated by one ring of adjacent faces at the coarsest level either touches, and its structure is none that the target's exact inverse or re-application would meet where §2.7's laws would not then hold (§2.7's laws, law 4)." 2. §7.1's undo row (l. 11306): "an `undo` or `redo` whose target has dependent live events (§7.4 *Independence*)" → "an `undo` or `redo` whose target has dependent live events (§7.4 *Independence*; among them each later live event whose structure its exact inverse or re-application would meet where §2.7's laws would not then hold, §2.7's laws, law 4)". 3. END at scope, T110-2 (4) (l. 19385-19386): after "and a hand `delete` of a run beneath a standing viaduct — the viaduct unchanged, no bend, the run back on its undo;" insert " an owner's `undo(h, of)` of a hand `delete` of the clause's standing aqueduct, after a later hand `drawWall` through where its supports stood with its channel there above the wall's top — refused `refuse.undo.dependent` naming the `drawWall`, nothing restored (§2.7's laws, law 4);".

issues.kind: READERS ('held' and 'locked' read without J147's shape axis)
issues.claim: The laws' *held* is 'locked, on the axis named' (l. 2653-2656) and law 1 (10) bars a meeting that changes a shape-held thing - 'an aqueduct merged into it, ... a gate made in it' (l. 2739-2743). Five hand-path sites of design text still say 'held' or 'locked' where only a placement-locked thing takes their outcome: §7.1 *Raised ways* (l. 11145-11146) 'in a held wall too, the fate *reshaped*', where *Carried way* gives a shape-locked wall no gate (l. 2790-2793), its aqueduct clause citing law 1 (2), (5), (6) but not (10) (l. 11149-11150); §7.1's bend.wall.raisedCrossing row (l. 11338) 'a held one's the fate *reshaped*'; V09 §4.20.2 (4) (V09 l. 3019) 'an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall, held or not, crosses it ... merged into it' and (l. 3033-3034) 'each the same with either side locked, pinned or neither, a held thing's change shown as the fate *reshaped*'; V09 §5.5 (l. 3962) 'reshapes a locked one'. Read with J147's *held* each gives a shape-locked wall a gate or a merge. No hand op can make a shape lock before round 8 designs the op (Part A), so nothing built or tested changes now: minor. The lock op, its axes and its readers outside the family's meetings are J150's and are not reported.
issues.required_change: 1. §7.1 *Raised ways* (l. 11145-11146): "— in a held wall too, the fate *reshaped* (§2.7's laws, law 2 *Carried way*, law 4's (G2)) —" → "— in a placement-locked wall too, the fate *reshaped*, and in a shape-locked one none, the way re-routed through the nearest gate of that wall a way of its class may pass, else refused (§2.7's laws, law 2 *Carried way*, law 1 (10), law 4's (G2)) —"; and (l. 11149-11150) "(item 363; §2.7's laws, law 1 (2), (5), (6); law 2 (a), (c);" → "(item 363; §2.7's laws, law 1 (2), (5), (6), (10); law 2 (a), (c);". 2. §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 11338): "a held one's the fate *reshaped*, law 4's (G2)" → "a placement-locked one's the fate *reshaped*, law 4's (G2)". 3. END at V09: §4.20.2 (4) (V09 l. 3019): "an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall, held or not, crosses it" → "an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall, placement-locked or not, crosses it"; (V09 l. 3033-3034): "each the same with either side locked, pinned or neither, a held thing's change shown as the fate *reshaped*" → "each the same with either side placement-locked, pinned or neither, a placement-locked thing's change shown as the fate *reshaped* (a shape-locked one's never made: §2.7's laws, law 1 (10))"; §5.5 (V09 l. 3962): "reshapes a locked one" → "reshapes a placement-locked one".

issues.kind: WORDING (two readings of a hand op's F-WALL clause)
issues.claim: Law 2 (c) is by path (l. 2825-2836): by hand refused; at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation the stage's raised-way rung re-lays once with its search band widened to wall.barrierReachM; law 2 (a) bounds a pull by 'the pull's search band' (l. 2808-2809); Part P decided it so (PRB7C-LCK-05, adjudication-r7.md l. 2980). §5.2's F-WALL row (l. 9852) places the hand clause after the rung's widened re-pull - 'a hand op that runs F-WALL — a hand contractWall, a terrain stroke's cliff re-anchor — is refused refuse.raised.meeting once its own re-pull fails' - and W1's last column repeats 'a hand op refused once its own re-pull fails' (l. 3340); read there, 'its own re-pull' is the rung's widened one, so a hand contractWall whose pull finds no lawful shape in its band is laid by one build through a band widened to wall.barrierReachM and refused by another. Both keep law 1 and the owner rules and no bar sets the case up (T110-2 (4)'s hand contractWall, l. 19407, crosses lawfully): minor.
issues.required_change: 1. §5.2's F-WALL row (l. 9852): "a hand op that runs F-WALL — a hand `contractWall`, a terrain stroke's cliff re-anchor — is refused `refuse.raised.meeting` once its own re-pull fails, never a stage left unwalled (§2.7's laws, law 2 (c))" → "a hand op that runs F-WALL — a hand `contractWall`, a terrain stroke's cliff re-anchor — takes no rung of it: it is refused `refuse.raised.meeting` once its own pull, within its own search band, finds no lawful shape, its band never widened and never a stage left unwalled (§2.7's laws, law 2 (a), (c))". 2. END at model, the crossing table's W1, its last column (l. 3340): "a hand op refused once its own re-pull fails, never a stage left unwalled (law 2 (c))" → "a hand op refused once its own pull, within its own search band, finds no lawful shape, its band never widened and never a stage left unwalled (law 2 (a), (c))".

issues.kind: CATALOGUE (a castle bent by hand for a raised way has no row cause and no line)
issues.claim: The fixed-place sentence gives a castle sited or resized by hand (setAttr(castle, 'site' | 'baileyArea'), T3) one outcome: its claim moved whole to the nearest lawful site, or its area to the nearest lawful value, measured back along the drag, else refused (l. 3251-3254). §7.1's refuse row names the refusal (l. 11339), but no bend row names the bend: the bend.wall.raisedCrossing row's causes (l. 11338) list strokes, re-traces, re-sections and gates, and the catch-all (l. 11341) only 'a place's site', so the key a builder emits and V09's words are unstated - bend.place.site (V09 l. 1974) is S10b's, with a Put it here anyway button no castle has. The outcome is the laws'; only the key and line differ (VF7-HND-03's class): minor.
issues.required_change: 1. END at determinism, §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 11338), its cause: after "or a `placeGate` or a gate's slid crossing where §2.7's laws bar a gate there (law 1 (5))," insert " or a castle sited or resized by hand (`setAttr(castle, 'site' \| 'baileyArea')`) whose claim §2.7's laws bar there (law 1 (6))," (the cell's `\|` the design text's `|`); its outcome: after "its stub or way following, the trace unchanged;" insert " a castle's claim moved whole to the nearest lawful site, or its bailey to the nearest lawful area, measured back along the drag (§2.7's laws, law 2 (a), law 3; its worked example the fixed-place sentence);". 2. V09 §4.9's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` (V09 l. 2104): after its fixed-place form 'for a fixed place moved, "The {anchor \| water gate} keeps clear of {way}, {m} m along the {edge}."' add ' — and, for a castle moved or resized by hand clear of {way}, "The castle keeps clear of {way}, {m} m from where you put it."'; and in its source cell, after "or a `placeGate` or a gate's slid crossing inside its under-deck strip where no gate may stand (law 1 (5))," insert " or a castle sited or resized by hand (the fixed-place sentence),".
